row.title: Independence-inducing binarizations for the three-symbol distribution
row.statement:
Let $X,Y,Z$ have the distribution specified in the source, with $Z$ determined by $X$ and $Y$ according to the displayed table. For $N\geq1$, let $\overline{Y^N}$ be any binary output of a binarization channel applied to $Y^N$, and let $\overline{Z^N}$ be an output obtained by processing $Z^N$. The **independence-inducing binarization conjecture.** For every $N\geq1$ and every $\overline{Y^N}$, there exists $\overline{Z^N}$ such that

$$
(X^N \perp\!\!\!\perp \overline{Y^N})\mid \overline{Z^N}.
$$

This strengthens the preceding bound-secrecy reduction by disallowing Alice from binarizing. The source presents it as a possible route to proving bound secrecy for the displayed distribution.
row.source_name: Andrey Boris Khesin, Andrew Tung and Karthik Vedula, “New Properties of Intrinsic Information and Their Relation to Bound Secrecy”, arXiv:2308.09031 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09031

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2023). “This open problem can be stated as follows.”

row.title: The Tokareva–Shapovalov conjecture on balanced Boolean functions as bent derivatives
row.statement:
Let $f$ be a balanced Boolean function in an even number $n$ of variables, of degree at most $n/2-1$. Suppose that there is a nonzero vector $y$ such that

$$
f(x)=f(x\oplus y)
$$

for every vector $x$.

**Tokareva–Shapovalov conjecture.** The function $f$ is a derivative of a bent function.

The paper states that this conjecture is disproved by constructing balanced Boolean functions satisfying the stated conditions that are not derivatives of bent functions.
row.source_name: Vladimir N. Potapov, “Existence of balanced functions that are not derivative of bent functions”, arXiv:2309.04244 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04244

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

row.title: Eventual stability of party trees for ultimate leader pairs
row.statement:
An **ultimate leader pair** is a limiting leader pair in the follower dynamics, and its **party tree** is the tree of followers associated with that pair. A party tree is **stable** after step $k$ if its graph structure no longer changes at any later step.

**Ultimate-leader-pair stability conjecture.** For every ultimate leader pair, there exists a step $k$ after which the party tree of the ultimate leader pair is stable.

This is a more specific long-term formulation of the claim that branching cannot persist outside the root. The source does not provide a proof or resolution.
row.source_name: Natasa Dragovic and Francois Baccelli, “On the Poisson Follower Model”, arXiv:2309.04864 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04864

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

row.title: Gharakhloo–Welker positive matching conjecture for complete 3-uniform hypergraphs
row.statement:
Let $H=(V=[n],E)$ be a complete $3$-uniform hypergraph. For integers $l_1$ and $l_2$, define

$$
E_{l_1,l_2}=\\{\\{a,b,c\\}\in E\mid a<b<c,\ a+b=l_1,\ b+c=l_2\\}.
$$

A subset $M\subseteq E$ is a **positive matching** if it is a matching and there exists a weight function $w:V\to\mathbb{Q}$ such that

$$
\sum_{i\in e}w(i)>0\quad\text{if }e\in M,\qquad \sum_{i\in e}w(i)<0\quad\text{if }e\in E\setminus M.
$$

**Gharakhloo–Welker's conjecture.** For every $3\leq l_1\leq 2n-3$ and $5\leq l_2\leq 2n-1$, $E_{l_1,l_2}$ is a positive matching.
row.source_name: Marie Amalore Nambi and Neeraj Kumar, “On Positive Matching Decomposition Conjectures of Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2309.15424 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15424

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

row.title: Validity conjecture for reciprocal-distance weight functions on augmented hypercubes
row.statement:
For a positive integer $n\geq 3$, let $Q_{n-1}$ be the $(n-1)$-dimensional hypercube, and let $G_n$ be the graph obtained by attaching a root $r$ to an arbitrary vertex of $Q_{n-1}$ through an extra pendant edge. Let $d(v,r)$ denote graph distance from $v$ to $r$, and define a weight function $w_n$ on $G_n$ by

$$
w_n(r)=0,\qquad w_n(v)=\frac{1}{d(v,r)}\quad\text{for all }v\neq r.
$$

**Validity conjecture.** The weight function $w_n$ is valid.

This claim concerns the construction of non-tree weight functions used to obtain pebbling bounds for hypercubes. The supplied text does not state whether the claim has been proved or remains open.
row.source_name: Marshall Yang, Carl Yerger and Runtian Zhou, “Lollipop and Cubic Weight Functions for Graph Pebbling”, arXiv:2310.00580 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00580

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: The set-uniform Vinogradov mean value conjecture
row.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be a finite set. For $s,k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $J_{s,k}(A)$ denote the number of solutions $(x_1,\ldots,x_{2s})\in A^{2s}$ to

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{s}(x_i^j-x_{i+s}^j)=0 \qquad (1\leq j\leq k).
$$

**Set-uniform Vinogradov mean value conjecture.** For every real number $\epsilon>0$,

$$
J_{s,k}(A) \ll_{s,k,\epsilon} |A|^{\epsilon}\left(|A|^s+|A|^{2s-k(k+1)/2}\right).
$$

This conjecture would replace the known factor $N^{\epsilon}$ in the corresponding bound for sets $A\subseteq[N]$ by the intrinsic factor $|A|^{\epsilon}$. The $k=1$ case is trivial, but even the $k=2$ case remains open according to the source.
row.source_name: Samuel Mansfield and Akshat Mudgal, “A Quadratic Vinogradov Mean Value Theorem in Finite Fields”, arXiv:2310.02950 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02950

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Moreover, while the $k=1$ case of this is trivial, unlike , even the $k=2$ case of this remains open.”

row.title: The domination-to-clique cluster conjecture
row.statement: For a tournament $T$, let $\operatorname{dom}(T)$ be its domination number and let $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T)$ be its clique number. **The domination-to-clique cluster conjecture.** There exist two functions $f$ and $\ell$ such that, for every integer $k$, every tournament $T$ with $\operatorname{dom}(T)\geq f(k)$ contains a subtournament $X$ with $|X|\leq\ell(k)$ and $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(X)\geq k$. The paper notes that this lies between the known domination-to-dichromatic cluster theorem and the stronger domination-to-domination cluster conjecture; it remains open.
row.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian, Pierre Charbit and Raul Lopes, “Clique number of tournaments”, arXiv:2310.04265 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04265

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: The local-to-global conjecture for tournament clique number
row.statement: For a tournament $T$, let $N^+(v)$ denote the out-neighbourhood of $v$, and let $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T)$ denote the clique number. **The local-to-global clique-number conjecture.** There exists a function $g$ such that, for every integer $t$, if $T$ is a tournament such that for every $v\in V(T)$, $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(N^+(v))\leq t$, then $\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T)\leq g(t)$. This is presented as the clique-number analogue of a known local-to-global theorem for dichromatic number and remains open.
row.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian, Pierre Charbit and Raul Lopes, “Clique number of tournaments”, arXiv:2310.04265 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04265

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: Conjecture that cube-width is at most the poset size
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite poset, and let $w^*(\mathcal P)$ denote its cube-width, as defined in the paper. The antichain shows that $w^*(\mathcal P)$ can be as large as $|\mathcal P|$.

**Cube-width conjecture.** For every finite poset $\mathcal P$,

$$
w^*(\mathcal P)\le |\mathcal P|.
$$

The paper reports that this bound holds for all posets considered there, while the general case is left open.
row.source_name: Paul Bastide, Carla Groenland, Maria-Romina Ivan and Tom Johnston, “A Polynomial Upper Bound for Poset Saturation”, arXiv:2310.04634 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04634

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: Existence conjecture for binary upcycles of diamondicity one
row.statement:
An upcycle with parameters $(a,n,d)$ is an upcycle whose alphabet size, word length, and diamondicity are respectively $a$, $n$, and $d$. Here $k$ is an integer parameter, and the claim concerns binary upcycles with diamondicity one.

**Binary upcycle existence conjecture.** There exist upcycles with parameters

$$
(a,n,d)=(2,2^k,1)
$$

for every $k\ge2$.

The question arises because all currently known upcycles can be constructed starting from binary upcycles with $d=1$, and the divisibility condition $n\mid da^{n-d}$ forces a binary upcycle with $d=1$ to have $n=2^k$ for some $k\ge2$. The supplied text says that only the cases $n=4$ and $n=8$ are currently known to exist, so the assertion remains open.
row.source_name: Dylan Fillmore, Bennet Goeckner, Rachel Kirsch, Kirin Martin and Daniel McGinnis, “The Existence and Structure of Universal Partial Cycles”, arXiv:2310.13067 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13067

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: Engbers–Erey–Fox–He conjecture for chromatic polynomials of l-connected graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic $l$-connected graph on $n$ vertices, where $k\geq 4$ and $l\geq 3$, and let $P(G,x)$ denote its chromatic polynomial. **Engbers–Erey–Fox–He conjecture.** For every $x\geq k$,

$$
P(G,x)\leq (x)_k(x-1)^{n-l-k+1}+O\big((x-2)^n\big).
$$

This is a proposed extension of the preceding chromatic-polynomial bounds from $2$-connected to $l$-connected graphs. The source says that the case $x=k$ was proved, while the displayed estimate for all $x\geq k$ is presented as a conjectural generalization.
row.source_name: Yan Yang, “Some results on the maximal chromatic polynomials of 2-connected k-chromatic graphs”, arXiv:2310.16382 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16382

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

row.title: Cochordality conjecture for higher independence hypergraphs
row.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and for each integer $r\geq 1$ let $\mathrm{Con}_r(G)$ denote the hypergraph defined by the $r$-independence construction. A graph is **cochordal** if its complement is chordal, and a hypergraph is cochordal if its complement is chordal. **Cochordality conjecture.** For all $r\geq 1$, $\mathrm{Con}_r(G)$ is a cochordal hypergraph if $G$ is a cochordal graph. This conjecture proposes a hypergraph analogue of Fröberg's theorem for higher independence complexes; the paper reports that it is based on calculations, and no resolution is given here.
row.source_name: Priyavrat Deshpande, Amit Roy, Anurag Singh and Adam Van Tuyl, “Fröberg's Theorem, vertex splittability and higher independence complexes”, arXiv:2311.02430 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02430

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: The infinite sumset conjecture in the primes
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ denote the set of prime numbers.

**Prime bounded finite-sums conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\left\{\sum_{n\in F}n:F\subset B,\ 0<|F|\leq k\right\}\subset\mathcal P-1.
$$

The analogous assertion holds with $\mathcal P-1$ replaced by $\mathcal P+1$. The conjecture is conditionally obtainable from the Dickson–Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, while the unconditional statement remains open; fixed shifts other than $\pm1$ are ruled out by the source's discussion.
row.source_name: Bryna Kra, Joel Moreira, Florian K. Richter and Donald Robertson, “Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond”, arXiv:2311.06197 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06197

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2023). “The case $k=2$ of , which corresponds to a slight variation of , is proved in .”

row.title: Cocycle expansion for quotients of Bruhat–Tits buildings with permutation coefficients
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple $p$-adic Lie group of rank $d\geq 3$, let $p\geq p(d)\gg0$, let $\Gamma$ be a lattice in $G$, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be the Bruhat–Tits building associated with $G$. The notation $h_1({}_\Gamma\setminus^\mathcal{B},{\rm Sym})$ denotes the relevant first cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients.

**Cocycle-expansion conjecture.** For every such lattice $\Gamma$,

$$
h_1({}_\Gamma\setminus^\mathcal{B},{\rm Sym})>0.
$$

This would establish cocycle expansion with permutation coefficients for quotients of Bruhat–Tits buildings of high-rank simple $p$-adic Lie groups, a proposed next step beyond the paper’s analysis of large cosystoles and property $(\tau)$.
row.source_name: Michael Chapman and Alexander Lubotzky, “Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open problems”, arXiv:2311.06706 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06706

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: The divisibility conjecture for even hook numbers in self-conjugate partitions
row.statement:
Let $a_h^*(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $h$ among self-conjugate partitions of $n$. **The even-hook divisibility conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq0$ and every integer $m\geq1$,

$$
a_{2m}^*(n)\equiv0\pmod{2m}.
$$

This predicts systematic divisibility for the even-hook counting functions of self-conjugate partitions. The source restates it as a conjecture from prior work, and no resolution is given in the supplied text.
row.source_name: William Craig, Madeline Locus Dawsey and Guo-Niu Han, “Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in restricted partitions”, arXiv:2311.15013 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.15013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: Intermediate-value conjecture for orientable total domination numbers
row.statement:
Let $G\in\mathcal{C}$ be a graph, and let ${\rm dom}_t(G)$ and ${\rm DOM}_t(G)$ denote its lower and upper orientable total domination numbers. For an orientation $f$ of $G$, write $G_f$ for the resulting oriented graph and $\gamma_t(G_f)$ for its total domination number. **Intermediate-value conjecture.** For every integer $c$ satisfying

$$
{\rm dom}_t(G)\leq c\leq {\rm DOM}_t(G),
$$

there exists an orientation $f$ of $G$ such that

$$
\gamma_t(G_f)=c.
$$

This extends the corresponding result known for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs. The source attributes the conjecture to the authors of the cited earlier work, and no resolution is given here.
row.source_name: Sarah E. Anderson, Tanja Dravec, Daniel Johnston and Kirsti Kuenzel, “Orientable total domination in graphs”, arXiv:2311.16307 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: The relative fractional packing characterization by graph expansion
row.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $[?]$ for the relative fractional packing number of $G$ with respect to $H$, and let $Expand(H)$ be the family of graphs obtained from $H$ by repeatedly removing vertices, adding edges, or replacing a vertex by a clique of arbitrary size. **Relative fractional packing conjecture.**

$$
\alpha^{*}(G|H) \leq 1 \quad\text{if and only if}\quad G \in Expand(H).
$$

The forward implication would characterize exactly when the relative fractional packing number is at most one in terms of the three graph-expansion operations; the reverse implication was already established in the preceding theorem. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.
row.source_name: Mehrshad Taziki, “Relative Fractional Packing Number and Its Properties”, arXiv:2311.16390 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16390

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: Conjecture that interval and integer Schur numbers coincide
row.statement:
Let $S(r)$ be the least positive integer $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ contains a monochromatic solution to $x+y=z$, and let $I(r)$ be the supremum of the real numbers $T>1$ for which the half-open interval $[1,T)$ admits a sum-free $r$-colouring. **Interval Schur number conjecture.** For all $r$, we have

$$
I(r)=S(r).
$$

The equality would make the bounds for $I(r)$ match up to logarithmic factors. The supplied text presents this as a belief and gives no resolution.
row.source_name: Lucas Aragão, Jonathan Chapman, Miquel Ortega and Victor Souza, “On the number of monochromatic solutions to multiplicative equations”, arXiv:2311.18742 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18742

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

row.title: Preperiod conjecture for extensions of subtraction sets of size at most three
row.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite subtraction set with $|A|\leq 3$, let $S\in\{0,1\}^{\alpha}$ be a seed, and write $p=\operatorname{Per}(A,S)$. An integer of the form $kp+x$ is an **extension** of $A$ for every $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$ and $x\in A$ under the condition stated. **Preperiod-extension conjecture.** If $kp+x$ is an extension of $A$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}_+$ and $x\in A$, then

$$
\operatorname{PrePer}(A,S)=0.
$$

The statement is the converse of the cited invariant-extension proposition for sets of size at most three. The source notes that it suffices to check $k=1$, and that the converse is not true for nonempty seeds in the unrestricted setting.
row.source_name: István Miklós and Logan Post, “Superpolynomial period lengths of the winning positions in the subtraction game”, arXiv:2312.02426 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02426

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023). “It is a long time open question if exponential period lengths exist in the substraction game. Alth\"ofer and B\"ultermann conjectured that superpolynomial period lengths might exist if $|A| \ge 5$ .”

row.title: Ballantine–Burson–Craig–Folsom–Wen divisibility conjecture for self-conjugate partition hook lengths
row.statement:
Let $a_t^{\star}(n)$ denote the number of hooks of length $t$ among all self-conjugate partitions of $n$. For integers $n\geq0$ and $m\geq1$, define divisibility in the usual sense. **Ballantine–Burson–Craig–Folsom–Wen conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq0$ and $m\geq1$, we have

$$
a_{2m}^{\star}(n)\equiv 0 \pmod{2m}.
$$

This is one of three conjectures of Ballantine, Burson, Craig, Folsom and Wen concerning the hook-length statistic $a_t^{\star}(n)$ for self-conjugate partitions. The supplied source does not state whether this divisibility conjecture has been resolved.
row.source_name: Tewodros Amdeberhan, George E. Andrews, Ken Ono and Ajit Singh, “Hook lengths in self-conjugate partitions”, arXiv:2312.02933 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02933

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).
